title: Smarter Faster Better: The Secrets of Being Productive in Life and Business
author: Charles Duhigg
target_audience: Anyone interested in behavioral science and the psychology of achievement
core_themes: The science and psychology behind productivity
Absorbing and acting on information efficiently
primary_purpose: To demystify productivity by uncovering the science and habits that make individuals and organizations more effective, offering actionable strategies for improving focus, motivation, decision-making, and overall results.

structure_format.organization: Divided into eight principle-based chapters, each spotlighting a productivity concept illustrated through real-life stories and research
features: Case studies from organizations, companies, and high performers
Actionable summaries and takeaways at the end of each chapter

key_concepts_lessons: Productivity is more about making choices on how to think than simply working harder.
Motivation increases when people feel a sense of control and autonomy.
Setting well-formed goals—especially using stretch goals and SMART goals—drives better outcomes.
Focusing attention deliberately (cognitive closure) prevents distraction and error.
Teams thrive when psychological safety exists and members feel comfortable taking risks.
Effective decision-making is fostered by mental models and scenario planning.
Managing how we absorb and use information is critical to learning and innovation.
Constructive use of data and self-reflection enhances performance over time.
style_tone: Balanced between scientific rigor and practical advice
notable_features: Blends storytelling, accessible science, and practical advice
Draws on research from psychology, neuroscience, and organizational studies
Examples from a wide variety of sectors—business, aviation, education, military, entertainment
Suggested actions and reflections at the end of each chapter
cultural_historical_context: Published during a renewed societal focus on workplace efficiency and individual achievement, the book addresses productivity in the technology era, synthesizing findings from the productivity movement, behavioral economics, and recent studies on motivation and teamwork.
reception_impact: Became a New York Times bestseller
Praised for combining captivating storytelling with actionable insights
Widely cited by business leaders, HR professionals, and productivity enthusiasts
Some critiques mention that the anecdotal nature can overshadow systematic methodologies
comparable_titles: The Power of Habit by Charles Duhigg
Getting Things Done by David Allen
